behavioral_effects: A user can create, list, patch, and delete coding workspaces from Settings -> Workspaces; each carries a backend_kind, an opaque server-generated sandbox id, an optional repo_url, a ruleset, and an auto_approve flag
The strict/auto-approve contradiction is refused, and auto_approve is cleared on a readonly workspace because ADR-006 registers no write or execute tool there — one owner for the rule, in the service
compatibility_impact: Additive. New table (workspaces), new endpoint family /api/v1/me/workspaces with its two proxy handlers, new settings route. One shared signature widened compatibly: core.sanitize.strip_url_credentials gains a keyword-only keep_path=False, so all seven existing callers are unaffected (test_ssrf.py green, 46 tests). Migration 0031 chains onto 0030 as the single head. No response shape or existing contract changed.
follow_up: Session A: pydantic-ai-backend CodingToolkit reading workspace.ruleset/auto_approve, ENABLE_CODING, workspace_id on the chat turn, frontend toggle; security-review before its record
Validate repo_url for SSRF at clone time, in the session that implements cloning
Sandbox service (sandboxd) as its own Compose service under the ADR-005 posture; decide ADR-006 open question 2 (egress) there
The same COUNT-without-pagination round trip exists in mcp_connection.list_for_user and user_slash_command.list_for_user
limitations: Shrink pass ran (4 parallel reviewers over the session diff) and changed the code: dropped the redundant clear_repo_url flag across 6 files in favour of explicit null + exclude_unset; removed the unreachable schema-level strict validator so the service is the single owner; deleted the never-read eager user relationship (McpConnection needed lazyload() to undo the same join); removed the COUNT round trip from an unpaginated list; folded the duplicated IPv6/netloc stripper back into core.sanitize; adopted the existing SectionCard, IconButton, and getErrorMessage instead of three new local copies; deleted an unreachable toast guard

Shrink pass findings deliberately NOT applied: the create-path get_by_name pre-check (the documented pattern in .claude/rules/architecture.md, kept alongside the IntegrityError race guard); the route-level 409/404/204 tests (mandated by the endpoint-fullstack skill); a generic useEntityList hook (would require migrating use-mcp-connections and use-slash-commands in the same change); a proxyToBackend helper (repo-wide, 47 handlers); a Ruleset StrEnum (deferred to Session A, where tool-registration code will actually switch on it)

Inherited debt not fixed here: window.confirm instead of ConfirmDialog, and hardcoded English instead of next-intl — both match every sibling settings manager; fixing only workspaces would make it the odd one out

No browser or Playwright check was run: the settings page is verified by vitest and by the generated site-chain report (boundaries.json now records the page reaching 4 backend route modules through its proxy handlers), not by driving a browser
reason: ADR-006 makes a coding workspace the thing a chat turn names, but nothing in the data model can hold a user-owned sandbox identity, its repository URL, or its ruleset, so no turn can reference one; this adds the workspaces table and its full-stack CRUD so later sessions can attach tools to a workspace id rather than to a deployment-wide default.
risks: auto_approve is stored but unenforced until Session A attaches the coding toolkit; a workspace can be marked auto-approving before anything can act on it
repo_url is not SSRF-validated at write time by design; the session that implements cloning must validate at clone time or the stored URL becomes an SSRF vector
rollback: git revert restores the code. The migration is already applied to the developer database: run 'alembic downgrade 0030_mcp_url_origin_only' (inside the app container — the host cannot reach Postgres) before or after reverting, which drops the workspaces table and any rows in it. Nothing else outside the repository is touched.
security_impact: New user-supplied URL surface: repo_url. Stored with userinfo, query string, and fragment removed via core.sanitize.strip_url_credentials(keep_path=True), restricted to the shared WEBHOOK_ALLOWED_SCHEMES allowlist, so a clone token cannot reach the row. SSRF validation is deliberately NOT performed at write time (it resolves DNS and the URL is not fetched here) — it belongs at clone time and is a named follow-up for the session that implements cloning; until then no code reads repo_url. Rows are user-scoped with a CASCADE FK, and every service path authorizes through get_for_user, which raises NotFoundError rather than revealing another user's workspace. No tool, file, shell, or sandbox capability is added by this session; auto_approve is stored but nothing reads it yet.
summary: Add the workspaces entity: model, migration, service, /api/v1/me/workspaces CRUD, proxy handler, and typed client
